suggested_services_note: Each row is one way this kind of work takes money (one of the master's 28 paths per flow). The owner keeps the services that fit and picks ONE path per service and place. Names and amounts are examples from the profession file, not prices.

suggested_services.name: Cremation and memorial
suggested_services.example: The main story: a free arrangement meeting with Helen. The family picks only what they want from the price list: direct cremation, a memorial service and an urn, $2,585. Rosie texts a bill for the $1,000 deposit when they sign, and one for the $1,585 rest before the service day.

suggested_services.name: Cremation and memorial
suggested_services.example: The same free meeting. The family pays the chapel its own way: a deposit on its card reader when they sign and the rest before the service, or from an insurance policy the chapel handles in its own tools.

suggested_services.name: Planning-ahead meeting
suggested_services.example: A free planning-ahead meeting with Helen, a licensed seller, about Alex's own wishes. Nothing is taken, and nothing is paid through Rosie: any plan is the chapel's own contract.

suggested_services.name: Funeral and burial
suggested_services.example: The main story: a free arrangement meeting at the family's home with Henry, the morning after he brought Alex's mother into the home's care. The family picks a funeral and burial from the price list: $6,130, with the first call's $395 on it. Rosie texts a bill for the $2,000 deposit when they sign, and one for the $4,130 rest before the service day.

suggested_services.name: Funeral and burial
suggested_services.example: The same meeting at home. The family pays from an insurance policy, which the funeral home handles in its own tools. Rosie texts no bill.

suggested_services.name: Planning-ahead meeting
suggested_services.example: A free planning-ahead meeting at Alex's own home with Henry, a licensed seller. Nothing is taken, and nothing is paid through Rosie: any plan is the home's own contract.

before_times: Has someone died, or is this about planning ahead?
Where did the death happen: a hospice, hospital or care home; at home under hospice care; or at home, not expected? (the safety check)
At the funeral home, by phone or video, or at your home?
Burial, cremation, or not sure yet? Only if the family wants to say.
after_time: Your relationship to the person who died, only if not said already
Who else shares the decisions, like a spouse, brothers or sisters? Names only.
Did they have a plan with any funeral home? Yes, no or not sure.
secure_page_only: The name of the person who died, and the date and place of death
The cause of death and any medical details, only if the director needs them
Their Social Security number, only if the family wants to give it ahead (otherwise in person)
The family's money details: an insurance policy, how they'll pay
Is it safe to text you? If not, how should the home reach you?
intake_questions.who_may_book: An adult family member or friend may book the meeting. Who has the right to make the decisions is a switch from the state's form (like a named agent, then a spouse, then adult children). The director confirms it at the meeting before anything is final. Planning ahead: the adult it's for, or someone they name.

stop: A death at home that was not expected, or not under hospice care: 911 first, and nobody is moved until the authorities say so
Someone may still be alive, or a medical emergency: 911
go_on: A death at home under hospice care: the hospice nurse first, no 911. Then the first call is sent now to the director on call.
A death at a hospice, hospital or care home: its staff call the funeral home the family picks. The meeting can be booked now.

what_rosie_says.not expected, at home: I'm so sorry. Please call 911 now. Nobody should move them until the authorities say so. When you're ready, we can set up a meeting.
what_rosie_says.at home, under hospice: I'm so sorry. Please call your hospice nurse first; there's no need to call 911. Then the home's director on call can come, any hour.
what_rosie_says.in a hospice or hospital: I'm so sorry. The staff there will call the funeral home you choose. A meeting can be set for tomorrow.

prep: Only if you have them: the birth date and place, the parents' names, and any military discharge papers. Bring them; please don't text them.
Any plan or insurance papers, and clothing if you wish. The director helps with the rest.
required: None before an arrangement meeting can be booked.
The first call happens on its own clock: sent now, any hour, never waiting for a meeting.
A death at home that was not expected: nothing is booked until the authorities say the person may be moved.

skills: The first call (bringing someone into care)
Planning ahead (a preneed seller's license where required)
Embalming (a licensed embalmer, only with permission)
staff.licenses_or_certificates: Each funeral director's own license where the state's rules require one: a switch from the state's form. Rosie never books work beyond it.
staff.supervision: An apprentice or intern only while their licensed director is working, where the state's rules allow it.
staff.who_oks: Sam OKs prices made for one family; lines straight from the price list need no OK. Sam's answer wins.
staff.stand_in: Another licensed director at the same home, offered by the home; the family picks by name.
staff.on_call: A director on call every night, weekend and holiday, with a backup. The first call reaches them right away, 5 minutes each.

children_and_age.who_may_book: An adult family member or friend may book the meeting. Who has the right to make the decisions is a switch from the state's form (like a named agent, then a spouse, then adult children). The director confirms it at the meeting before anything is final. Planning ahead: the adult it's for, or someone they name.

visit.check_in: At the funeral home: the code at the front desk. Phone or video: the director asks for the code at the start. At the family's home, or for the first call: the code at the door.
visit.done: The code, or DONE with the statement.
visit.changes_at_visit: Anything added later, like more death certificates or another urn, is priced from the list before it's done.

license.note: Optional. Upload anything. Rosie never checks it and never shows it as checked (D96).
license.need: Always, where the state's rules require it: the funeral home's own establishment license, and each funeral director's own license. A crematory license where the home runs its own crematory and the state's rules require one. Planning ahead: a preneed seller's license where the state's rules require one. All of it comes from the state's form.
license.who: The funeral home; each funeral director; each preneed seller, where the state's rules require it.
license.ask: The home's establishment license number at sign-up. Each director's license number in their invite reply. A preneed seller's license number where it applies.
license.insurance: Any bond or insurance the state's form asks for, on file before going live.

never_in_a_text: The cause of death, or any medical detail
The Social Security number of the person who died
The family's money details: insurance, payment
None of these in texts to the owner or staff either
